Maria Claudia, Tom Reilly here, following up on this morning's call. First of all, thank you. That was the clearest update we have had on the Pittsburgh line, and two of the partners told me so afterwards. Two things. To begin with, the rerouting through Paranagua has the go-ahead from our side, and your mandate on the forwarder's rate stands at twenty-six hundred dollars. If you can get it lower, even better. Having said that, one of the partners asked me whether the backup suppliers would be able to meet our quality standard, and I told him I did not know. It seems to me that is the first question you should put to them, before price. Finally, when you sound them out, please spell out that this is not a tender yet. We are not looking to replace Pittsburgh this year. Call me when you have the rate.

Three months ago, I needed a colleague on every call with our partners abroad. Today I ran one on my own, and I want to be honest about what worked and what did not. What worked was the structure. I opened with one sentence, I signposted every part, and nobody asked me where we were. What worked less well was the numbers. Twice I said a figure too fast, and I had to repeat it. The questions were the part I was most afraid of, and they turned out to be the part I did best. When I was asked whether I could guarantee the date, I did not say yes. I said it was likely, and I spelled out what it depended on. If I had given that answer three months ago, it would have been in Portuguese, in my head, and it would have arrived too late. Next block, I want to work on one thing only: the pace of my numbers.

First, before the meeting, you sound out one person to learn what the others are worried about. Then, you write the outline around the one decision you need from the room. After that, you give the update: a hook, three signposted points and a call to action. Next, you answer the questions, conceding what is true and hedging what you cannot promise. Finally, you follow through: you do what you promised, and you report back by the date you gave.
